title: Approximate inference capacity tradeoffs - regional SLA worksheet
content:
SUMMARY:
This worksheet explores tradeoffs between low-bit (8-bit, 4-bit) inference and batching strategies across three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) with a focus on meeting 99th-percentile latency SLAs for interactive products while maximizing throughput and minimizing GPU hours. The goal is to produce a small set of operational knobs (batch size, async queue depth, backfill pool sizing, and quant profile) for QE and SRE to experiment with in the next two quarters.

OBJECTIVES:
- Produce per-region GPU capacity recommendations for three quality buckets: baseline (fp16), approx-8bit, approx-4bit.
- Estimate SLA breach probability under workload spikes and plan backfill/overflow pools.
- Surface expected quality delta (approx. relative RMSE / human-eval delta) and map to routing policy suggestions.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (conservative):
- Target SLA: 99th <= 350ms for single-turn chat (prompt + gen).
- Average request size: 120 input tokens, expected generation: 40 tokens.
- Model family: open-llama-13B class with similar KV-cache characteristics.
- Host hardware: A100-80GB for baseline; T4-equivalent for low-cost backfill.
- Effective throughput scaling: int8 => 1.8x tokens/sec vs fp16, int4 => 2.6x tokens/sec vs fp16 (measured for our runtime with KV cache and batching).
- Quality delta (approx human-eval): int8: ~1.8% quality loss, int4: ~4.5% average loss on our internal eval set (task-dependent).

WORKLOAD PROFILES:
- Stable interactive: 120 qps peak, p50 latency target 90ms, p99 SLA 350ms.
- Burst window: 30s spikes up to 2.5x baseline traffic.
- Background batch/async: reranks and embeddings run during off-peak but may be throttled during bursts.

SCENARIO TABLE (per-region, snapshot):
Columns: region | model | quant | baseline tokens/sec (per GPU) | est tokens/sec (quant) | default batch | eff RPS (requests/sec) | est GPUs needed (p99 headroom) | est cost / hour (USD) | quality_delta | notes

Rows:
us-west | fp16 | n/a | 48k | 48k | 8 | 360 | 9 | 36.0 | 0% | baseline; small fleet, stable latency
us-west | int8 | 8-bit | 48k | 86.4k | 12 | 540 | 5 | 20.0 | -1.8% | higher batch improves amortization; p99 sensitive to queueing
us-west | int4 | 4-bit | 48k | 124.8k | 16 | 780 | 3 | 12.0 | -4.5% | aggressive; suitable for best-effort traffic/backfill
eu-west | fp16 | n/a | 44k | 44k | 8 | 330 | 10 | 40.0 | 0% | slightly lower throughput due to instance types
eu-west | int8 | 8-bit | 44k | 79.2k | 12 | 495 | 6 | 24.0 | -1.9% | prefer for paid-tier customers with strict latency guardrails
eu-west | int4 | 4-bit | 44k | 114.4k | 16 | 714 | 4 | 16.0 | -4.6% | use as overflow/backfill; monitor regressions

ap-southeast | fp16 | n/a | 42k | 42k | 8 | 315 | 11 | 44.0 | 0% | small regional fleet; cold-start risk higher
ap-southeast | int8 | 8-bit | 42k | 75.6k | 12 | 468 | 7 | 28.0 | -2.0% | cost-effective for regional 99SLOs if combined w/ cache
ap-southeast | int4 | 4-bit | 42k | 109.2k | 16 | 684 | 5 | 20.0 | -4.8% | consider for daytime batch augmentation

Notes on table calculations:
- baseline tokens/sec is measured per-GPU token throughput for fp16 under our runtime, normalized to comparable sequence lengths.
- est tokens/sec for quant = baseline * quant_speedup_factor (int8: 1.8x, int4: 2.6x).
- eff RPS = (est tokens/sec) / (avg tokens per request). avg tokens per request = (120 + 40) = 160 tokens.
- est GPUs needed = ceil(desired_capacity_rps / eff_RPS_per_gpu). desired_capacity_rps= target p99 headroom traffic (e.g., 120 qps stable, 300 qps peak). We provision to support 2.5x burst with 1.2x safety margin.
- est cost per hour uses committed A100 rate for baseline ($4/hr) and discounted rate for approx pools, pro-rated by GPU count (these rates are placeholders and should be replaced with actual procurement prices).

SLA AND QUEUEING MODEL (back-of-envelope):
- p99 latency is modeled as service_time + queue_delay. Service_time inversely scales with tokens/sec. Queue_delay grows non-linearly with queue depth; above 60ms queuing budget we see p99 breach in our test harness.
- For int8 with larger batch sizes, service_time drops but queue_delay increases; net p99 may improve only if we cap queue depth and keep a low-latency fast-path for small requests.

SUGGESTED OPERATIONAL POLICY (per-region):
1) Two-tier routing:
   - Fast-path (fp16, conservative batching): 60% of interactive traffic, strict p99 budget.
   - Economy-path (int8/int4): 40% of traffic, routed by customer tier / feature flag; int4 primarily for non-critical features and background jobs.
2) Dynamic backfill pools: maintain a small fleet of int4 instances for overflow and batch processing (size = daily_offpeak_batch_work_units / 12 to finish within 2 hours).
3) Canary policy: progressive rollout of int8 model for specific customer segments; measure quality delta on live prompts using sampling (1% of requests) and automated regressions.
4) Autoscaler knobs: prefer vertical scale (batch size increase) up to p95 latency threshold; beyond that spin up additional GPUs.

RISK REGISTER (short):
- Quality regressions: int4 may fail on instruction-following edge cases; mitigation: real-time regression alerts + auto-fallback to fp16 for flagged prompts.
- Cold-start and warmup: adding int4 pods reduces mem pressure but increases fragmentation; mitigation: pre-warmed pools separate from on-demand.
- Cost leakage: aggressive batching hides capacity shortages until peak; mitigation: enforce explicit p99 SLAs in cost dashboards and set reactive alerts.

QUANTITATIVE SENSITIVITY (quick experiments to run):
- Sweep: batch size = [8, 12, 16, 20] x quant profiles = [fp16, int8, int4] for 24h in us-west; capture p50/p95/p99 and regression rate.
- Spike tests: 2.5x, 4x, 6x for 30s windows; measure time-to-recover and p99 breach fraction.
- Quality A/B: route 5% of production traffic to int8/int4 with human rater sampling for 48h; quantify delta on high-sensitivity prompts.

RECOMMENDATIONS (immediate):
- Start a 2-week canary in us-west running int8 with bounded queue depth (max 12) and sampling for regressions.
- Allocate an int4 backfill pool of 6 GPUs in ap-southeast to handle nightly batch demand and short-term overflow during regional spikes.
- Add a new dashboard tile in Console: "Approx inference: quant vs p99" showing per-region p99 vs cost per GPU-hour and flagged regression rate.

NEXT ACTIONS / TODOs:
- [Aisha] Prepare canary rollout plan + Linear ticket linking to GH-PR-987 (due 2026-07-09).
- [Marco] Run batch sweep in staging and upload results to CONFLUENCE-12345 (due 2026-07-16).
- [Emily] Implement sampling hooks and a quick human-rating UI to capture quality deltas (due 2026-07-12).
- [SRE] Create alert for p99 deviation > 25% when running int8 canary (JIRA-INFRA-4123).

ATTACHMENTS / DATA SNIPPETS:
- Recent microbenchmarks (May-Jun 2026) show int8 speedup variance +/-6% depending on avg seq length.
- Small CSV snippet (tokens/sec per GPU):
  us-west,fp16,48000
  us-west,int8,86400
  us-west,int4,124800

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Which customer-facing endpoints should be allowed on int4 by default? (security/review alignment needed)
- Do we want to expose a pricing tier that corresponds to economy-path (int8/int4)?

END OF SHEET
